statement.before:
Let $s$ be space-constructible and $s'(n)=o(s(n))$. Then
$$\mathrm{DSPACE}(s'(n))\subsetneq\mathrm{DSPACE}(s(n)).$$
There is no logarithmic factor here (unlike time): a universal machine simulates any other with only a constant-factor blow-up in space. For example $\mathrm{DSPACE}(n)\subsetneq\mathrm{DSPACE}(n^2)$, and $\mathrm{DSPACE}(\log n)\subsetneq\mathrm{DSPACE}(\log^2 n)$ for $s(n)=\log^2 n$ (here the $o$ is taken with care for tiny bounds).
statement.after:

There is no logarithmic factor here (unlike time): a universal machine simulates any other with only a constant-factor blow-up in space. statement.after:
There are oracles $A$ and $B$ such that

$$\begin{gathered}\mathrm P^{A}=\mathrm{NP}^{A}\\
\text{and}\quad \mathrm P^{B}\neq\mathrm{NP}^{B}.\end{gathered}$$

Take $A$ to be any $\mathrm{PSPACE}$-complete language (e.g. TQBF); then $\mathrm P^A=\mathrm{NP}^A=\mathrm{PSPACE}$. Take $B$ built by diagonalization so that $L_B=\{1^n:\ B\cap\{0,1\}^n\ne\emptyset\}$ is in $\mathrm{NP}^B$ but not in $\mathrm P^B$. Consequently a proof of $\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}$ or of $\mathrm P\ne\mathrm{NP}$ cannot be *relativizing*, i.e. cannot be one that holds verbatim for every oracle — which rules out plain simulation-and-diagonalization arguments.

statement.before: Let $\mathrm{HALT}_1=\{1^n : \text{the } n\text{-th Turing machine halts on the empty input}\}$ be the unary halting language. It is undecidable, yet $\mathrm{HALT}_1\in\mathrm{P/poly}$: the advice for length $n$ is the single bit $a_n=1$ iff $1^n\in\mathrm{HALT}_1$, and the machine first rejects strings containing 0, then outputs $a_n$ on $1^n$. More generally every unary language lies in P/poly (the advice is again one bit per length), so P/poly is uncountable and contains languages outside every class of decidable languages.
statement.after: Let $\mathrm{HALT}_1$ be the unary language consisting of $1^n$ exactly when the $n$-th Turing machine halts on the empty input. It is undecidable, yet $\mathrm{HALT}_1\in\mathrm{P/poly}$: the advice for length $n$ is the single bit $a_n=1$ iff $1^n\in\mathrm{HALT}_1$, and the machine first rejects strings containing 0, then outputs $a_n$ on $1^n$. More generally every unary language lies in P/poly (the advice is again one bit per length), so P/poly is uncountable and contains languages outside every class of decidable languages.
